propositions: The plan-review gate's LLM-as-judge exhibits self-consistency drift across repeated Pass-2/Pass-3 runs on the same findings, threatening the stability of new sub-answers like asserted_capability_confirmed routed to G6/E4/T3 cohort

Section-order permutation of plan text causes verdict flips (PASS↔BLOCK or PASS↔INDETERMINATE), violating the expected stability of absolute rubric scoring before R3 lands a new order-exposed container criterion
Experiment A measures Fleiss' κ and raw agreement on pass3_decide decision output over 50 G6/E4/T3 findings × 3 self-consistency votes, passing iff κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8 (R5 prerequisite)

Experiment B measures Fleiss' κ and raw agreement on gate verdict over 14 permutable plans (≥3 top-level sections) × 3 distinct deterministic section-order permutations, passing iff κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8 (R3 prerequisite)

Infra-INDETERMINATE outcomes (llm_unavailable or verify_failed flags on coverage) are excluded and re-run as execution failures, not stable judge decisions; genuine unsupported-stack INDETERMINATE is retained as an agreement category
